verdicts.correction: The program is illegal on its own under §13.18.16.3 SR5 (checked: 'The entry specified by data-name-1 shall not have an occurs-depending table subordinate to it' -> OK §13.18.16.3 5)). CT OCCURS 0 TO 5 DEPENDING ON NN is subordinate to CG. The .err code COBOLNET1699 is the SR5 arm (report-control-operand-shape), as the writer says. An implementation that ignores GR6 completely still rejects this source with exactly the same code, so the negative pins SR5 and not GR6. Check (d) fails as well: the program is not otherwise legal, so GR6 is not the only reason it is rejected. The writer's own note says every zero-length group that can be known at compile time also falls under SR5 or SR7, so no compile-time golden can isolate GR6. Drop the test-ref and route the row to not-closable or an owner adjudication. Do not cite 1699 as GR6's witness.

The 85 golden writes 'COPY l1c04_copy_spacing'. Its text-name is a user-defined word that contains UNDERSCORES. The underscore is a COBOL-2002 word character: constructs.json user-word-underscore-2002 (§8.3.2.1) says the '85 set is hyphen-only. So the program uses a construct that does not exist in 85 and cannot sit in tests/conformance/85. The compiler accepts it only because the COPY text-name bypasses the word gate, which is a gate hole and not a licence. Rename the copybook to a hyphen-only name (e.g. COPY L1C04-COPY-SPACING with file L1C04-COPY-SPACING.cpy). Alternatively move the golden to 2002. A literal text-name is not an option, because that form is also post-85. The expected stdout itself is right ('[A  B.C]', '[X,Y;]', '[P  Q]', '[ B]'), and the 2002 partial-word golden (N=AAA T=BBB D=CCC) is correct as it stands. The row's test_ref becomes valid once the 85 file is fixed.

Arithmetic (14.7.7 r1): -5.625 under ----9.999 gives '   -5.625'; 37.96875 rounds to 37.97; -3.333 truncates to -3.33; 17.125 truncates to 17.1; 87.5+3.75 = +0091.25; 10.125/-7 = -1.446 rounds to -01.45. 14.7.7 r4: I re-read 4a/4b. The ADD TO initial evaluation covers only the operands before TO. Line 6 identifies the receiver T(I) after I=3, so TG=202. Line 7's imperative runs after the stores (14.7.5 r3). The line 9 REDEFINES overlap gives 12/12. CORR r3/r5: I checked each namesake against rules 1-5. BWZ is numeric-edited in 85 as well. G3R's own REDEFINES does not exclude K, because it is not a group subordinate to D1. INITIALIZE: I checked GR5c 2/4 to confirm REPLACING alone leaves the other categories untouched. Index: MOVE to an implicit index item is the only violation, and an implementation that skipped the implicit usage would fail with a different code (missing PICTURE). CONSTANT RECORD: VALUE in the linkage and file sections is legal (13.7 GR5, 13.18.63), so SR1 is the only reason those two are rejected; the 2002 edge follows constructs.json constant-record-2002. National: 2 bytes per DOC-A.1-213; the UTF-8 bytes in the .out are correct. I ran cite.py --check on all 28 distinct citations and every one returned OK at the stated clause.
